- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline or delay correction until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate upward momentum — reduce forecast slope or add mean-reversion term.
- Model frequently underestimates true price range in early 30-day horizon — increase forecast by 1–2% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.5 to -0.5 in 3 days), model often misjudges direction — align forecast with sentiment median over 3-day window instead of 1-day trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70) after a spike, model often fails to recognize — add 1–2% downward bias in forecast for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early forecast days — use sentiment variance as weight to adjust forecast smoothness (e.g., higher variance → more volatile forecast).
